My family has 16.1 mu of flat land here in Quzhou, and we grow cotton — that's what our village does, same as my neighbors. I've been managing these fields for five years since my mother-in-law handed them to me, and with six people in the house we have enough hands for the spraying and picking that cotton demands. I don't read books about farming, but I watch what works. My neighbor across the road plants guoxinmian every year and gets good bolls, so I buy that improved seed too — about 2.5 jin per mu. I hire the village rotary tiller in mid-April to break up the soil, then I lay plastic mulch to keep the heat and moisture in, and sow around April 20th when the ground warms up. For fertilizer, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — roughly 50 kg of the 15-15-15 kind from the co-op — and when the plants start flowering I topdress with urea to give them a push. I pump from our well three times: at sowing, at flowering, and during boll filling. Water costs money for electricity, so I don't overdo it, but three times is what my mother-in-law always did. The biggest worry is pests. Cotton bollworm, aphids, and red spider mite come every summer without fail, so I spray insecticide about twelve times from June to August, plus herbicide twice and maybe a growth regulator. I expect around 550 jin of seed cotton per mu if the weather holds — about what I harvested last year.
